insights.headline: Gold slips on MCX as dollar, yields climb; central bankers reaffirm gold's reserve role
insights.summary: MCX gold futures fell nearly 1% to about ₹1.49 lakh per 10g as the US dollar touched an 18-month high and Treasury yields stayed elevated, while silver gained to ₹2.27 lakh per kg. At the LBMA's annual conference in Sorrento, the Bank of Italy's deputy governor and the Bundesbank president said gold remains a strategic reserve asset despite surging bond yields, flagging a structural shift since 2022. The GST Council may scrap the 3% tax exemption on bullion imports by banks and nominated agencies, and soft US payrolls have cut October Fed hike odds to 22%.
points: MCX gold fell ~1% (₹1,020) to ₹1.49 lakh/10g on a stronger dollar; silver rose 0.5% to ₹2.27 lakh/kg.
Bank of Italy's Altimari told the LBMA meet gold is 'probably the safe haven asset'; Bundesbank's Nagel backed gold diversification.
GST Council may withdraw the 3% bullion-import tax exemption for banks and nominated agencies, raising landed costs.
Weak US payrolls cut October Fed hike odds to 22%; spot gold held near $4,160 while the dollar index hit 102.5.
Jewellers expect strong festive buying despite shifting patterns: lighter pieces, old-gold exchange, budget-first buying.

trending.title: Dollar and yields vs gold: the tug of war
trending.summary: A surging dollar and elevated yields cap gold even as weak US jobs data cools Fed hike bets; the dollar's latest gain is Europe-driven, and Deutsche Bank's Ghali calls gold oversold and underowned.

trending.title: Central banks anchor gold's structural bid
trending.summary: At the LBMA's Sorrento conference, top central bankers called gold 'probably the safe haven asset' and flagged a structural shift since 2022 — even as the industry's rule-setter fights for survival.

trending.title: Policy watch: GST break and the rupee
trending.summary: The GST Council may scrap the 3% bullion-import tax exemption for banks while the RBI is seen intervening to support the rupee — both shift landed gold costs for Indian buyers.

trending.title: Festive demand meets record prices
trending.summary: Jewellers expect strong festive buying despite changing consumer patterns — lighter pieces, old-gold exchange and budget-first spending — even as Q2 jewellery volumes fell 15% while value rose 34%.

trending.title: Silver's $55–$60 line in the sand
trending.summary: Silver is testing key support between $55 and $60 after Friday's jobs-led swings, with US rates the deciding factor; analysts see demand emerging at these levels.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 1%, silver gains on MCX: What is driving bullion prices
items.summary: MCX gold futures slipped about 1% — ₹1,020 per 10g — to ₹1.49 lakh as the US dollar climbed to an 18-month high of 102.37 and Treasury yields stayed elevated, while silver rose 0.54% (₹1,223/kg) to ₹2.27 lakh per kg; international spot gold held steady near $4,163.50 an ounce.

items.title: Gold retains key reserve status despite surging bond yields, central bankers say
items.summary: Bank of Italy deputy governor Altimari told the LBMA's Sorrento conference gold remains "probably the safe haven asset", flagging a structural shift since 2022 from emerging-economy central-bank buying. Bundesbank chief Nagel said the case for gold diversification stands despite rising yields; Metals Focus sees 2026 central-bank demand easing 15% to 720 tonnes, still above pre-2022 levels.

items.title: GST exemption for banks, nominated agencies for gold, silver imports may be withdrawn
items.summary: The GST Council is likely to consider withdrawing the 3% IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies at its Oct 7 meeting, sources said. The relief dates to 2017, when bullion trade was tightly canalised; scrapping it would put banks, nominated agencies and bullion exchanges on the same tax footing, after import duty was hiked to 15% in May.

items.title: RBI likely intervenes to support rupee, traders say
items.summary: The rupee held at 96.24 to the dollar on Monday as state-run banks were seen selling dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, four traders told Reuters. The move helped the currency withstand a broadly stronger dollar - the dollar index hit a more than one-year high of 102.5 - and volatile oil prices. A weaker rupee keeps imported gold and silver costlier for Indian buyers.

items.title: Gold gains as October Fed rate hike prospects fade
items.summary: Spot gold edged up to $4,158 an ounce on Monday after weaker-than-expected US September jobs data cut the market-implied odds of an October Fed rate hike to 22% from 64% a week earlier, per CME FedWatch. Silver gained 1.7% to $61.40. Analysts note December tightening is still largely priced in, capping gains.

items.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD languishes below $4,200 amid high US yields
items.summary: FXStreet notes spot gold trimmed losses but stays pinned below $4,200 with last week's $4,110 floor close by; soft US jobs data has futures pricing an 80% chance the Fed stands pat in October, up from 30% a week ago, though elevated Treasury yields keep a floor under the dollar. Its technical read puts near-term resistance at $4,230.

items.title: Why Gold and the Dollar are rising together today
items.summary: FXStreet's Przemyslaw Radomski explains today's unusual joint rally: the dollar's gain is driven by euro weakness (euro at 1.116 on French fiscal worries), not US rates, while cheaper oil eases long-end yields — the channel gold follows. Gold near $4,196 is an oversold bounce after a 3.6% weekly drop; he warns the trend still hinges on US long-term yields.

items.title: Deutsche Bank's Ghali says gold oversold and underowned in interview
items.summary: Deutsche Bank's head of metals research Daniel Ghali told BNN Bloomberg that gold is oversold and underowned, noting it has held above its July lows even with 10-year US yields above 5% and oil above $100 a barrel; he added that CTA funds hold their largest net-short gold position and central banks keep buying quietly, while cautioning silver could underperform on oversupply.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast 05/10: Tests Key $55–$60 Support Zone
items.summary: DailyForex analyst Christopher Lewis says silver stays volatile as interest-rate markets and energy inflation drive trading. Friday's weak US jobs report (29,000 vs 90,000 expected) briefly lifted silver before it fell back; the metal now sits on $55–$60 support where he sees demand, with US rates the key driver into the weekend.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Strong Dollar and High Yields Put $50 in Focus
items.summary: Silver lost more than 6% last week and stays under pressure, with high US Treasury yields and a strong dollar capping any recovery, according to FXEmpire's analysis. The piece argues silver needs lower real yields and a weaker dollar to sustain a rebound; a break below the $60 support would put the $50-$55 zone in focus, while a move back above $62.60 could open the way to $67.

items.title: Bullion faces choppy week as dollar, US-Iran risks test sentiment: Analysts
items.summary: Analysts expect gold and silver to stay turbulent next week as a strong dollar and high Treasury yields clash with unresolved US-Iran tensions; the RBI's rate decision on Wednesday is the other key cue. Last week MCX gold fell about 2% to ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams and silver about 4% to ₹2.25 lakh per kg; Comex gold dropped 3.7% to $4,162.3 an ounce.

items.title: Risks for $1 trillion-a-week gold market as rule-setter LBMA fights for survival
items.summary: The LBMA, which sets the rules for London's $1 trillion-a-week gold market, is fighting a London court case that insiders fear could leave it insolvent, investingLive reports. At stake are the Good Delivery List and the responsible-sourcing regime underpinning global bullion trade. The report lands as the market debates the long-term survival of the gold market's key rule-setter.

items.title: Gold Nears ₹1.5 Lakh per 10 Grams as India Heads into Its First 15% Duty Dhanteras
items.summary: At ~₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams this is the most expensive Dhanteras on record, and the first under the 15% import duty. The premium decomposes neatly: $4,140/oz at a rupee near 96.3 gives ~₹1.28 lakh landed parity, and 15% duty plus 3% GST add most of the rest. WGC Q2 data: jewellery volumes fell 15.4% while bars and coins rose 8.9%; loans against gold jewellery surged 83% to ₹5.6 lakh crore.

items.title: Festive season outlook: Jewellers expect strong buying despite changing consumer patterns
items.summary: CNBC-TV18 reports jewellers expect strong festive and wedding-season buying even as high gold prices change how consumers buy: lighter, lower-carat, versatile pieces within defined budgets, traction for old-gold exchange, and more room for diamonds. WGC: Q2 jewellery demand fell 15% YoY to 75 tonnes while value rose 34%; CRISIL sees 20–25% revenue growth for organised retailers this fiscal.

items.title: Will the Festive Season Revive Gold Jewellery Demand as Prices Stay Elevated? What Shoppers Are Doing Differently
items.summary: With Dhanteras and Diwali approaching, Indian gold jewellery demand is holding up even at elevated prices - but shoppers are changing how they buy, reports Kalkine India's Anjali Anand. Buyers are choosing smaller grammage, lighter designs and staggered purchases rather than walking away from gold. The piece tracks the shifting festive buying trends as prices stay near record highs.

items.title: Gold, silver lose lustre in September
items.summary: Both precious metals posted negative September returns as a stronger dollar and US rate-hike expectations dented sentiment: Comex gold fell 6.8% to $4,189.1 an ounce and Comex silver 9.6% to $60.75. On MCX, gold dropped 4.1% to Rs 1,49,092 per 10 grams and silver 6.8% to Rs 2,23,740 per kg - the rupee's weakness against the dollar softening the domestic fall.
